summary.text: Frank Mrvan is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Indiana's 1st District, first elected in 2020 and seeking a fourth term.
A former mortgage broker and pharmaceutical sales representative, he served as North Township trustee for 15 years before Congress and sits on the House Appropriations Committee.

paragraphs.text: Mrvan was born and raised in Hammond, Indiana, graduated from Morton High School in 1987 and earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from Ball State University in 1992.
He worked as a licensed mortgage broker and pharmaceutical sales representative before entering elected office.
He was appointed North Township trustee in November 2005 when his predecessor resigned and served until 2021, a total his official biography describes as 15 years.

Mrvan announced his candidacy for Congress in 2020 after Rep. Pete Visclosky decided not to seek re-election, won a 14-candidate Democratic primary with 33% of the vote, and defeated Republican Mark Leyva in the general election, 57% to 40%.

He took office January 3, 2021, was re-elected in 2022 over Republican Jennifer-Ruth Green and in 2024 over Republican Randy Niemeyer, and defeated LaVetta Sparks-Wade in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the House Appropriations Committee and its Commerce, Justice, Science and Energy and Water Development subcommittees and is vice chairman of the Congressional Steel Caucus.
His earlier House assignments included the Veterans' Affairs Committee, whose Technology Modernization subcommittee he chaired in 2021–22, and the Education and the Workforce Committee.
According to his official biography, Mrvan is married to Jane and they have two daughters.
